story.title: Federal Reserve Set to Raise Interest Rates for First Time Since 2023
story.summary: The Federal Reserve is anticipated to increase interest rates for the first time in three years, a decision closely monitored due to rising inflation and consumer prices. This meeting is significant as it marks the first rate hike under the new chairman, Kevin Warsh.

explore_lenses.label: How did the Fed reach this point?
explore_lenses.title: Inflation data and a split July vote raised pressure
explore_lenses.summary: The prospective move follows an extended hold, renewed price pressures and public signals from Chair Kevin Warsh that the inflation outlook had not improved enough to justify staying put. The July decision also showed substantial internal support for tightening.

claims.text: The FOMC’s July 29 decision to hold rates was 9-3; Beth Hammack, Neel Kashkari and Lorie Logan preferred an immediate quarter-point increase.
Producer prices for final demand increased 0.4% in August and were up 5.4% over 12 months, according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics.
Warsh said at Jackson Hole that the Fed’s predominant focus should be prices; AP reported that he said underlying inflation had not meaningfully improved after the July meeting.
Kevin Warsh became Fed chair on May 22, 2026, after Senate confirmation; the FOMC unanimously selected him as its chair that day.

story_report.summary: Federal Reserve officials are widely expected to approve a quarter-point interest-rate increase at their September 15-16 meeting, which would be the first hike since 2023 and the first under Chair Kevin Warsh. Rising consumer and producer prices have sharpened the case for tighter policy: August consumer inflation reached 3.4% over 12 months, while producer prices rose 5.4%. A rate increase could raise some consumer and business borrowing costs, though the immediate effect on mortgages and other longer-term loans is less direct.

sections.heading: Federal Reserve Inflation Policy
sections.body: The Federal Open Market Committee held its federal-funds target range at 3.50% to 3.75% in July and said inflation remained elevated relative to its 2% objective. That decision split the committee 9-3, with Beth Hammack, Neel Kashkari and Lorie Logan favoring an immediate quarter-point increase. Warsh, who became chair on May 22 after Senate confirmation and a unanimous FOMC selection, has said the Fed’s predominant focus should be prices.

sections.heading: Borrowing Costs and Mortgage Rates
sections.body: A Fed increase can push up rates paid by consumers and businesses for borrowing. But mortgage rates and other longer-term rates do not necessarily move in lockstep with one policy decision because they are also driven by longer-term bond yields. The size and timing of any pass-through to household borrowing costs will therefore depend on lenders and market conditions as well as the FOMC’s action.

sections.heading: Rate Path and Political Pressure
sections.body: As of September 15, CME FedWatch odds cited by ABC News put the chance of a quarter-point hike at 94%. Wall Street investors anticipated three increases, potentially including moves in December and March, though UBS economist Jonathan Pingle said cooler inflation could let the Fed forgo additional hikes. President Donald Trump has favored rate cuts or no change, while adviser Kevin Hassett said Trump would defend Warsh’s independence even if displeased by an increase; the next scheduled FOMC meetings are October 27-28 and December 8-9.

unresolved.text: The FOMC had not released its September 16 policy statement when the evidence was prepared, so the final decision and its terms were not yet confirmed.
The number and timing of any further rate increases remain unsettled and depend on incoming inflation, employment and financial-market data.

related_stories.title: Supporting Acts Withdraw from Ed Sheeran's Tour Amid Macklemore Controversy
related_stories.summary: All four supporting acts for Ed Sheeran's US tour have withdrawn in solidarity with rapper Macklemore, who was dropped from the tour after making comments in support of Palestine. The artists who exited include Irish acts Aaron Rowe and Beoga, Danish band Lukas Graham, and American singer Finneas. They announced their decision on social media, highlighting their support for Macklemore amidst the controversy surrounding his remarks about Gaza.

related_stories.summary: Former Philippine President Rodrigo Duterte made his first appearance before judges at the International Criminal Court (ICC) in The Hague. The 81-year-old is facing accusations of crimes against humanity, with discussions regarding his health and memory impairment taking place during the session.

related_stories.title: Trump Critiques Supreme Court Justices Over Mail-In Voting Ruling
related_stories.summary: Trump expressed dissatisfaction with some Supreme Court Justices for their ruling on mail-in voting, which he believed did not align with his expectations. This ruling has provided clarity for voters and election officials ahead of the upcoming midterm elections, as it blocked the Trump administration from imposing new restrictions on mail ballots. The Supreme Court's decisions are seen as a setback for Trump's efforts to limit mail-in voting.
